Experiment Structure Overview

Custom experiments are divided into several sections.

Two objects are provided to every experiment.

  • core, which is an instance of core.Core.
  • config, which is an instance of Config.

Configuration

If graphical configuration is desired, this must be the first section in the script. To provide this functionality, the script is executed (with limited functionality) when the selected in the "Settings" section of the GUI. Available NMReady extensions are:

  • config:add()
  • ConfigItemNumber()

If any other NMReady extension is found, the configuration section is considered to be finished, so be sure to keep calls to config:add() at the top of your script.

firstTau = config:add(ConfigItemNumber("Tau Start: (ms)", {min="0.1", max="30000.0", default="1000", precision="2"}))

See config for more information

Setup: Display

See t1.lua for an example.

Setup: Acquisition parameters and pulse sequences

Setup must be performed before acquisitions. This includes setup of core parameters as well as the creation of custom pulse sequences. This can be done at any time after the configuration section. If the pulse sequence or any parameters are left unchanged, the defaults are equivalent to the 1D acquisition parameters currently set in the GUI.

pulse90 = core:channelConfigSignal():get90PulseSeconds()
pulse180 = pulse90 * 2
p = PulseSequence(core:channelConfigSignal())
p:add(newPulseSingle(core:channelConfigSignal()))
p:add(newPulseSingle(core:channelConfigSignal()))
p:setPulseTime(0, pulse180)
p:setPulseTime(1, pulse90)
core:usePulseSequence(p)

See core and pulses for more information.

Acquisitions

When the interpreter reaches the acquire() statement, a 1D acquisition is performed using the current pulse sequece and acquisition parameters (including the configured number of transients.)

The signal data is available as a DataSet1D object using Core:dataSetSignal().

Exporting and/or displaying results

After the acquire() statement, data is available for export and/or display.

If the display setup has already been done (see above), you can copy the recently acquired signal data to the location that will be used for the display. You will also have to let the GUI know that it should be updated immediately.

-- Set the data in displayResult
displayResult:set(core:dataSetSignal())
-- Send the data in displayResult to the GUI
updateDisplay(currentResult)

See display for more information.

If you would like to export 1D data, you can do so with the exportResults1D function:

exportResults1D(core:dataSetSignal(), "my_filename")

See data for more information, including how to store and export 2D results.
